items.title: Georgia Juvelis Leaving As Chief Communications Officer Of AMC Global Media After 19 Years With Company
items.summary:
Georgia Juvelis is stepping down as Chief Communications Officer of AMC Global Media at the end of the year, closing out a 19-year run at the company. She announced the move Monday in a memo to staff, which Deadline published in full.

AMC does not plan to hire a replacement. Instead, the company is dismantling its centralized communications structure, leaving each business unit's comms team to operate independently while coordinating with one another.

Juvelis joined the company in 2007, when it was still Rainbow Media and AMC was in the early stages of its shift from a classic movie channel to a home for prestige drama. In her memo she traced the chapters that followed: Mad Men and Breaking Bad, the ratings run of The Walking Dead, the 2011 public spin-off, the launch of AMC Studios, international expansion, and the streaming services AMC+, Shudder and Acorn TV. "It's been an honor to tell the company's story through these many chapters, raising our profile and ensuring our shows, films and talent got the recognition they so richly deserved," she wrote.

AMC Global Media CEO Kristin Dolan credited Juvelis with guiding the company's communications "through some of our most important moments" and called her a trusted colleague and partner. Juvelis thanked Dolan, the senior leadership team and former boss Josh Sapan, along with longtime communications colleagues Jim Maiella, Olivia Dupuis and Matt Pollack.

She ended the note on a personal symmetry: she was expecting her first child when she arrived at AMC, and is leaving having just dropped that daughter off at college. Her departure takes effect at the end of 2026.

items.title: ‘Coven Academy’ Renewed For Season 2 By Disney
items.summary:
Disney has ordered a second season of Coven Academy, the supernatural teen drama that premiered on Disney+ and Hulu roughly three weeks ago. The renewal came Monday, Deadline reported, on the back of early viewership figures the company was happy to publicize.

Disney said the first season has drawn 20.3 million global hours across Disney+ and Hulu in its first three weeks, plus more than 30 million additional views after the opening chapter was posted to TikTok, Instagram and YouTube. The series ranked as the No. 1 streaming show among teens 12 to 17 over premiere weekend and placed in the top five among all viewers 2 and up by views.

The co-viewing numbers were the other selling point. Per Nielsen, half of viewers aged 12 to 17 and close to two-thirds of children aged 6 to 11 watched alongside an adult, a pattern that matters for a title Disney is positioning as family programming rather than strictly teen fare.

Season 1 follows three teenage witches and a group of warlock classmates at an elite magic boarding school, where the coven is caught between long-running supernatural conflicts and forbidden romances. Malina Pauli Weissman stars as Briar, with Malachi Barton as Jake, Jordan Leftwich as Sasha, Ora Duplass as Tegan, Louis Thresher as Ollie and Tiffani Thiessen as Miss Graves. Devon Sawa guest-stars as Mr. Cole.

Tim Federle, who created High School Musical: The Musical: The Series and is behind the upcoming Romy and Michele sequel, created the show and executive produced the first season with Darren Swimmer, Todd Slavkin, Amanda Row and Bronwyn North-Reist. His Chorus Boy Productions produces in association with Disney Kids Family. Season 1 is streaming on Disney+, Hulu and Freeform On Demand.

items.title: Chris Brown Gets Suspended Eight-Month Sentence for ‘Vicious and Unprovoked’ Attack at U.K. Nightclub
items.summary:
A London judge handed Chris Brown an eight-month suspended sentence over an assault at a nightclub in February 2023, sparing the singer jail time. Judge Tony Baumgartner delivered the sentence at Southwark Crown Court, where Brown pleaded guilty in July to a single count of affray.

Brown's co-defendant, Florida rapper Omololu Akinlolu, who performs as HoodyBaby and whom the Crown Prosecution Service described as Brown's vocal coach, also pleaded guilty. He received a four-month sentence, suspended for 12 months.

The court heard that the two men attacked music producer Abraham Diaw at Tape London, with Brown striking Diaw twice on the head with a tequila bottle while Akinlolu punched him. "They continued their assault whilst the victim attempted to flee through the club," the CPS said. "The victim was kicked while he was seated defenseless on the floor."

Diaw went to a hospital with head and knee injuries, and a warrant was issued for both men, who had already left the United Kingdom. Brown was arrested in May 2025 after returning to the country for a world tour date in Manchester. Variety reported that additional charges, including assault, grievous bodily harm and a weapons count against Brown, were dropped after the men denied them.

Addressing Brown before sentencing, Baumgartner said he had weighed the singer's career but drew a line at what it buys him. "Your fame, commercial success and professional standing do not entitle you to special treatment," the judge said. "The law applies equally to everyone."
